scope: Private commuter shuttles that load/unload in San Francisco: regional tech/employer shuttles (SF <-> San Mateo / Santa Clara) and intra-city employer/institutional shuttles. Hospital/institutional shuttles that do not use the SFMTA program are mostly outside these counts.

headline.mostRecentPublishedRidership: No SFMTA ridership figure has been published since the 2017 Annual Status Report (Dec 2017 data). Permittees must report average daily boardings monthly (FY26-27 permit terms, Sec. IX.F.3), but the SFMTA does not publish them; the SF Chronicle (May 2026) says operators 'only have to report stop events'. Recent trend data are stop events and vehicles only.

preCOVIDRidership.note: SFMTA counts 'people who board' at SF program stops each day (one direction, roughly one boarding per commuter per day). The 2015 pilot figure of 17,000 'boardings' counts both directions (= ~8,500 people round-trip), so 8,500 people (2015) and 8,900 people (2017) are the comparable series. No 2019 ridership figure was found.

headline.trend: Vehicles: 469 AM / 463 PM average pre-COVID -> 172 AM / 132 PM in Nov 2021 (SFMTA FAQ); 415 AM / 385 PM in Feb 2020 -> 255 AM / 236 PM in July 2022 (-38%, SFMTA data via SF Examiner). Stop events: about 3,470/day Dec 2017 -> 1,503/day Oct 2021; 2026 year-to-date monthly stop events (article dated May 23, 2026) were 40% below 2019 (SFMTA data via SF Chronicle, May 2026) and had 'leveled off'.
headline.suggestedModelUse: Not a published number: if ridership scales with stop events, 2026 regional riders would be about 0.6 x the 2019 level. 2019 ridership itself is unpublished; Dec 2017 = 8,900 people/day.

acsClassification.finding: The Census Bureau gives no rule for employer or private shuttles. ACS Q32 (2023) asks for the ONE box 'for the method of transportation used for most of the distance', with options Car, truck, or van; Bus; Subway or elevated rail; Long-distance train or commuter rail; Light rail, streetcar, or trolley; Ferryboat; Taxicab; Motorcycle; Bicycle; Walked; Worked from home; Other method (questionnaire p.16). Subject definitions (2023, p.104) say 'Car, truck, or van' includes company cars but excluding taxicabs, and 'Public transportation' includes workers who used a bus, subway... or ferryboat. Neither mentions shuttles. So a shuttle rider classifies themself: most likely 'Bus' (counted under Public transportation in B08301), possibly 'Other method'. This is an inference, not stated by the Census Bureau.
